ZainCash support: architecture and ticket flow

Long image

A

Answer

ZainCash support uses one Jev classification path, with deterministic routing and a human approval boundary.

  1. Jev is the only ticket classifier; uncertainty remains an escalation reason.1
  2. Gemini is limited to extraction gaps and optional drafting, not classification.2
  3. PostgreSQL, policy retrieval, and the drafting agent support the same ticket journey.3

1 · System architecture

Diagram structure
  • Web + CLI entry entry
  • LangGraph pipeline
  • Jev jev-service
  • Support LLMs support-models
  • PostgreSQL database
  • Human review reviewer
  • entry → pipeline · tickets
  • pipeline → jev-service · classify
  • pipeline → support-models · extract + draft
  • pipeline → database · SQL + vectors
  • pipeline → reviewer · outcome
  • reviewer → database · audit

2 · Ticket flow

Diagram structure
  • Ticket received ticket
  • Prepare text prepare
  • Text present? text-check
  • Jev classifies jev-step-node
  • Verify + fill fields extract
  • Match transaction lookup
  • Apply routing rules decide
  • Draft + safety checks draft
  • Escalate empty empty-review
  • Human approval approve
  • decide → draft · reasons kept
  • draft → approve
  • extract → lookup
  • jev-step-node → extract
  • lookup → decide
  • prepare → text-check
  • text-check → empty-review · no
  • text-check → jev-step-node · yes
  • ticket → prepare
  1. Prepare text ↗

    Normalize text and mask card numbers.

  2. Jev classifies ↗

    Only Jev classifies. Low confidence remains attached for escalation.

  3. Apply routing rules ↗

    Python rules set team, priority, and escalation reasons.

  4. Human approval ↗

    A person approves, edits, or rejects. Nothing is sent automatically.
